description: Attribution lines that a mail client inserts above quoted reply history. Matching one of these is a structural anchor: it is the strongest single piece of evidence that everything following is embedded history rather than new content. Patterns are matched per line against the canonicalised plain text projection.

patterns.comment: Attribution line whose trailing 'wrote:' was wrapped onto the next line. Requires a date or clock time so that ordinary sentences beginning with 'On ' do not match, and is scored well below an anchor because it cannot be trusted alone. Measured firing on 10.4 percent of the corpus before the date requirement was added.
Lark Mail drops the space after On: 'OnTue, Sep 29, 2026, 12:15 <address> wrote:'. Anchored on a weekday name so ordinary words starting with On do not match.

Attribution without an On prefix, such as 'Bob Smith wrote:'. The lookaheads reject first person prose like 'As I wrote:' or 'Like I wrote:', which is the sender talking about themselves, not a client inserted attribution.

Two real shapes: 'Den <date> skrev <name>:' with the name after the verb, and the bare 'X skrev:' form matching the Estonian and Finnish family. The old '(Den|.{0,60})' alternation made Den dead and accepted any line with skrev anywhere before a colon.
The lookahead rejects first person prose such as 'как я писал:', which is the sender referring to themselves, not an attribution.
Yandex Mail's attribution: day first date, time, name and address, then a colon and no verb: '29.09.2026, 11:30, "Marta Kask" <address>:', or with the address in parentheses in a forward.
Catalan, as Roundcube writes it: 'El 2026-09-29 13:55, Marta Kask va escriure:'.
Galician, as Roundcube writes it: 'O 2026-09-29 11:46, Marta Kask escribiu:'.
Albanian, as Roundcube writes it: 'Më 2026-09-29 12:36, Marta Kask shkroi:'.

Bulgarian, Serbian and Macedonian, as Roundcube writes them: 'На 2026-09-29 12:28, Marta Kask написа:', 'Дана ... написа:'. Roundcube's Macedonian template ships unfilled ('На $дата,$праќач напиша:') and is still an attribution.
Croatian, as Roundcube writes it: 'Dana 2026-09-29 12:31, Marta Kask je napisao(la):'.

Ukrainian, Belarusian, Bulgarian and Serbian without an opener, verb followed by an optional date: 'Marta Kask напісаў 2026-09-29 12:28:', '... "Marta Kask" <...> написа:'. Requires a clock time on the line, since the bare verb also occurs in prose.
Greek: 'Στις 2026-09-29 11:47, Marta Kask έγραψε:'. Requires a clock time on the line, which attribution lines carry and prose rarely does.
Basque: '2026-09-29 11:43 egunean, Marta Kask-(e)k idatzi du:'. Requires a clock time on the line, which attribution lines carry and prose rarely does.

Finnish with the date after the verb: 'Marta Kask kirjoitti 2026-09-29 12:15:'. The older x_kirjoitti_fi only accepts the verb right before the colon. Requires a clock time on the line, which attribution lines carry and prose rarely does.
Dutch without the Op opener: 'Marta Kask schreef op 2026-09-29 11:46:'. Requires a clock time on the line, since 'schreef' is ordinary prose.

Danish and Norwegian without the Den opener: '"Marta Kask" <...> skrev 29. september 2026 kl. 10:10:', including SnappyMail's doubled colon. Requires a clock time on the line, which attribution lines carry and prose rarely does.
Icelandic: 'September 29, 2026 at 10:06 AM, skrifaði "Marta Kask" <...>:'. Requires a clock time on the line, which attribution lines carry and prose rarely does.

Chinese, simplified and traditional, with an ASCII or full width colon: '2026年9月29日 10:18, "Marta Kask" <...> 写到:'. Requires a clock time on the line, which attribution lines carry and prose rarely does.

Persian: '۷ مهر ۱۴۰۵ ساعت ۱۰:۰۳, "Marta Kask" <...> نوشت:'. The digit lookahead accepts Persian and Arabic-Indic digits. Requires a clock time on the line, which attribution lines carry and prose rarely does.
Arabic, as Roundcube writes it, verb first: 'كتب Marta Kask في 2026-09-29 11:43:'.
Hebrew, as Roundcube writes it, in logical order with the colon first: ':כתב Marta Kask, 2026-09-29 12:30 בתאריך'.

Cypht's attribution: date, name, address, then a verb with no colon, in many languages ('said', 'sagte', 'a dit', 'mengatakan', 'napisał(a)', ...): 'Am Tue, 29 Sep 2026 08:09:34 +0000Marta Kask marta.kask@example.com sagte'. Requires both a date and an address on the line, since without a colon the verb alone is prose.
Frisian, as Roundcube writes it: 'Op 2026-09-29 13:56, skreau Marta Kask:'.

patterns.pattern: ^\s*-{2,}\s*(Original Message|Originalnachricht|Message d'origine|Mensaje original|Messaggio originale|Oorspronkelijk bericht|Algne teade|Исходное сообщение)\s*-{2,}\s*$

patterns.comment: Welsh 'Ar 2026-09-29 14:04, ysgrifennodd Marta Kask:', Irish 'Ar an ..., scríobh Marta Kask:', Nynorsk 'Den ... skreiv Marta Kask:', Turkish '..., Marta Kask yazmış:', Uzbek 'Marta Kask yozgan kun 2026-09-29 14:04:'. Requires a clock time on the line, which attribution lines carry and prose rarely does.

Czech 'Dne 2026-09-29 14:24, Marta Kask napsal:', Slovak 'Dňa ... Marta Kask napísal(a):', Azerbaijani '2026-09-29 14:24 tarixdə, Marta Kask yazıb:'. Requires a clock time on the line, which attribution lines carry and prose rarely does.

More Roundcube translations: Bosnian 'je napisao/la:', Esperanto 'skribis:', Estonian '2026-09-29 14:26 kirjutas Marta Kask:', Persian 'نوشته است:', Faroese 'skrivaði Marta Kask:', Interlingua 'ha scribite:', Korean '쓴 내용:', Luxembourgish 'schreift:', Lithuanian 'rašė:', Marathi 'लिहीले :', Armenian 'գրեց.' (ending in a full stop), and Uyghur 'يازدى:', whose template ships unfilled. Requires a clock time on the line, which attribution lines carry and prose rarely does.
Malay as Roundcube writes it, with no colon: 'Pada 2026-09-29 14:27, Marta Kask menulis'. Anchored on the opener and a timestamp, since without a colon the verb alone is prose.
Roundcube's Uyghur attribution template ships with its placeholders unfilled: 'date$ دا، sender$ يازدى:'. The literal placeholders cannot occur in prose.

The 'Original Message' separator as Roundcube and SnappyMail translate it, collected from test/fixtures/clients. Roundcube uses it to introduce forwards, which the classifier turns into forwarded content when the subject marks a forward.

inlineAnnouncements.comment: 'my answers are inline', 'replies are inline', 'comments inline'. The sender says the reply is written into the quoted text.
'My comments below', 'Some replies below', 'see my comments below'. Requires a possessive or quantifier, because 'the answers below' in prose points at the sender's own text.
'Answers are in your letter', 'my comments are in your email'.
'Vastused on kirja sees' (the answers are inside the letter), 'panin oma mõtted sinu maili sisse' (I put my thoughts into your mail), with or without 'punasega' (in red).
'minu vastused.' as a short lead-in to answers typed into the quoted questions. Requires sentence end, because 'minu vastused Sinu küsimustele: 1)' introduces answers the sender wrote out in full.
